title: Normal tensor components realized as embedded joins
statement: Let $P$ be a normal integral domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(P)$, fix a separable closure $K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K$ [def-kun-separably-closed], and let $\mathfrak q_1,\mathfrak q_2\subset P$ be prime ideals. Put $H_i=P^h_{\mathfrak q_i}$ for ordinary henselizations [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] and $T=H_1\otimes_P H_2$. For each nonempty connected component $Z\subset\operatorname{Spec}T$, take its component ring $U=T/I_Z$ with $I_Z$ generated by the idempotents vanishing on $Z$ [lem-trf-affine-etale-cover-component-criterion]. Then $U$ is a normal integral domain, $P\to U$ and the two maps $H_i\to U$ are injective, and $\operatorname{Frac}(U)/K$ is separable algebraic. There is a $P$-embedding $U\hookrightarrow K^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Under this embedding $U$ is precisely the subring generated by the images of $H_1$ and $H_2$. Each canonical homomorphism $H_i\to U$ is ind-etale [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra].

source.place: Theorem 6.3, printed p. 13, normal-domain reduction and realization of a component in a separable closure; ind-etale factor maps also use the component-quotient argument of Tags 00EG and 097K. Online paper read; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-henselization-prime-ind-etale] to $(P,\mathfrak q_i)$: each structural map $P\to H_i$ is ind-etale. Base change in [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] makes $H_1\to T$ and $H_2\to T$ ind-etale, and composition makes $P\to T$ ind-etale. These are the specified tensor-factor maps, using the algebra tensor construction of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property].

Apply [lem-trf-component-ind-etale-local-henselian] to the chosen component $Z$: the actual quotient $T\to U$ is ind-etale. Compose with the maps of Step 1 using [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability]. Thus $P\to U$ and both $H_i\to U$ are ind-etale, proving the final assertion already. The component-ring clause of [lem-trf-affine-etale-cover-component-criterion] identifies the underlying space of $\operatorname{Spec}U$ with $Z$. In particular $U\ne0$ and its spectrum is connected. No assertion about henselianity of $U$ has been used.

Choose a small filtered presentation $U=\varinjlim B_\lambda$ by etale $P$-algebras, which exists by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Each $B_\lambda$ is a normal ring by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-over-normal-ring-normal]. The underlying ring diagram also has colimit $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-normal-ring] to conclude that $U$ is a normal ring. This asserts normality at prime localizations, and does not yet assert that $U$ is a domain.

In the same presentation, suppose $a,b\in U$ satisfy $ab=0$. The elementwise colimit statement [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] and filteredness give representatives $a_\lambda,b_\lambda$ in one stage; its equality clause lets us pass to a later stage at which $a_\lambda b_\lambda=0$. Apply [lem-trf-etale-normal-domain-finite-factors] to that stage to write it as a finite product of normal domains $C_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent], the only idempotents of $U$ are $0,1$: its spectrum is nonempty and connected, and these correspond to the empty and whole clopens. The images of the coordinate idempotents of the finite product are orthogonal and sum to $1$, so exactly one is $1$ and all others are $0$. If it is the $j$th one, the ring map from that stage to $U$ factors through $C_j$: every element of the other factors is its own product with an idempotent mapping to zero. In the domain $C_j$ the projected relation gives $a_{\lambda,j}=0$ or $b_{\lambda,j}=0$; hence $a=0$ or $b=0$. Together with $U\ne0$ this proves that $U$ is an integral domain.

source.place: Tag 030C (lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal), finite-stage decomposition; Tag 00EE, idempotents and clopens; filtered-colimit element and relation argument.

proof.text: Step 3 and the last sentence of [lem-weil-pbc-normal-domain-of-local-normal] show that the domain $U$ is integrally closed in $\operatorname{Frac}(U)$. Also each $H_i$ is a local ring by its henselization structure [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], and is an ind-etale $P$-algebra by Step 1. The local colimit theorem [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain], applied to its etale $P$-algebra presentation, therefore makes each $H_i$ a normal integral domain. Its hypothesis is a local colimit, not necessarily a strict henselization.

source.place: Tag 030B (lemma-normality-is-local); more-algebra.tex Tag 06DI, local filtered etale colimits.

proof.text: The maps $P\to U$ and $H_i\to U$ of Step 2 are weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], hence flat by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. For any one of their source domains $R$ and $0\ne r\in R$, multiplication $R\xrightarrow{r}R$ is injective. The definition [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], with the identifications $R\otimes_RU=U$, says that multiplication by the image of $r$ on $U$ is injective. If that image were zero, it would kill $1\ne0$ in $U$. Therefore each of the three ring maps is injective. In particular the structural map extends to $K\hookrightarrow L=\operatorname{Frac}(U)$.

source.place: proetale.tex Tag 097N (ind-etale implies weakly etale); flatness applied to multiplication by a nonzero element.

proof.text: Put $S=P\setminus\{0\}$ and $V=K\otimes_PU=S^{-1}U$. This identification sends $(p/s)\otimes u$ to $pu/s$, and the inverse sends $u/s$ to $(1/s)\otimes u$; the tensor relations and the localization fraction relation show these are inverse maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], base change makes $K\to V$ weakly etale. The map $V\to L$ is a localization: inverting all nonzero images $u/1$ of $u\in U$ gives fractions $(a/s)/(b/t)=at/(sb)$, precisely all fractions of the domain $U$, and the usual cross-multiplication equality is the same. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-localization-ring-weakly-etale] and composition in [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] make $K\to L$ weakly etale. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-field-separable] to these fields to conclude that $L/K$ is separable algebraic.

source.place: proetale.tex weak-etale base change/composition; more-algebra.tex Tag 092R (weakly etale residue field extensions).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-embeds-separably-closed] to the separable algebraic field extension $L/K$ and the fixed separable closure $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$, which is separably closed. It supplies a $K$-algebra embedding $L\hookrightarrow K^{\mathrm{sep}}$. Restrict it along the canonical inclusion $U\hookrightarrow L$ to get the required $P$-embedding. Composing with the injective maps of Step 6 gives the two stated embedded copies of $H_i$.

source.place: fields.tex Tag 09GU, separable version; Mathlib IsSepClosed.lift (FieldTheory/IsSepClosed.lean:294).

proof.text: Let $\jmath:U\hookrightarrow K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ be this embedding and let $J$ be the subring generated by the images of $H_1,H_2$ in it. The algebra tensor multiplication of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives $a\otimes b=(a\otimes1)(1\otimes b)$. Every element of $T$ is a finite sum of pure tensors, so its image under $T\twoheadrightarrow U\xrightarrow{\jmath}K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ lies in $J$. Surjectivity of the first map gives $\jmath(U)\subseteq J$. Conversely both images of $H_i$ lie in $\jmath(U)$, which is a subring, so $J\subseteq\jmath(U)$. This proves the claimed equality of subrings for the actual quotient maps.
